description: We are a small family team from Türkiye who love space, games and storytelling. We enjoy turning real science into something fun and easy to understand for kids. Our skills include coding, web development, game design, art and data analysis. We are excited to work with NASA's open data and learn as much as we can during the hackathon. Our team is complete, but we are always happy to chat and share ideas with other participants.
summary:
The day you play, the Sun in our game is the real Sun.

Mars Colony: Command Center is a free, fully voiced browser game where kids aged 7–12 command a Mars outpost and make the same trade-offs a real crew faces. Five story chapters replay real NASA events: Perseverance landing at Jezero, the 2018 dust storm that silenced Opportunity, the 2017 and 2024 solar storms Curiosity measured, and, in the final chapter, the Sun's real activity of the last 30 days from NASA DONKI.

Every challenge trade-off becomes a hands-on mission: keep the oxygen maker in the green (life support), save the greenhouse (food), fold the panels before the dust wall (power), turn the dish to find Earth (communication delay) and rush the crew into the shelter (radiation). The Earth–Mars message delay is calculated from today's real orbits, and every number links to its NASA source.

Why it matters: our study of 14,788 app-store reviews found that only 8 of 594 kids' apps even mention NASA, and ads are a top complaint. So we built it fun first, science inside, with no ads, purchases or accounts. Two kids on our team playtested every build.
details:
THE DAY YOU PLAY, THE SUN IN OUR GAME IS THE REAL SUN.

Mars Colony: Command Center is a free, fully voiced Mars mission trainer for kids aged 7–12. Its final chapter asks NASA what the Sun actually did in the last 30 days, and turns every real solar flare, CME and particle storm into a decision the young commander must make for the crew. No two months play the same, because no two months of space weather are the same.

▶ Play (no login, any device): Mars Colony: Command Center

💻 Source code + 4 sprint reports: GitHub

🖥️ Presentation: Canva

📊 Reproducible market research (Colab): Colab notebook

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. WHY WE BUILT IT: WE STARTED WITH DATA, NOT IDEAS

Before drawing a single character, we wrote a Colab notebook that scraped and analysed 14,788 public reviews and 840 app listings from Google Play and the App Store, in the US and Türkiye, in English and Turkish. What we found shaped every design decision:

• Only 8 of 594 kids' app listings even mention NASA → every chapter in our game is a real NASA event, and every number has a source.

• 25% of 1–2★ reviews of Mars and space games complain about ads → no ads, no purchases, no timers, no account.

• Good kids' reviews say "fun" 8× more often than "learn" → the science lives inside the play, never as a lecture.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

2. WHAT IT DOES: FIVE REAL EVENTS, FIVE REAL TRADE-OFFS

The player creates a commander and leads a crew they come to care about (Aylin the biologist, Deniz the engineer, Kerem the doctor) with NOVA, the base AI who explains the science out loud. Each chapter replays something that really happened:

Ch. 1 · Landing at Jezero – Perseverance's 2021 landing; start the oxygen maker modelled on MOXIE; grow lettuce on the ISS timeline (OSDR OSD-268)

Ch. 2 · The Dust Wall – the 2018 global dust storm that ended Opportunity (sky opacity tau 0.5 → 10.8); keep the base alive on almost no solar power

Ch. 3 · The Late Warning – the Sept 2017 solar storm that doubled radiation on Mars; Earth's warning arrives minutes late, using today's real light delay

Ch. 4 · The Biggest Storm – May 2024, Curiosity RAD's largest reading (8,100 micrograys); a crew member is outside, what do you do?

Ch. 5 · Today's Real Sun – live NASA DONKI events from the last 30 days

Every challenge trade-off becomes a hands-on mission, not a quiz:

• Life support → keep the oxygen maker's needle in the green

• Food → save the greenhouse plants before they fade

• Power → fold six solar panels before the dust wall hits

• Communication delay → turn the dish until you find Earth

• Radiation shielding → rush the crew into the shelter / race the rover home

Mission scores feed back into the simulation (air, food, power, shielding, science, radiation dose), so skill changes the story.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

3. HOW IT WORKS: REAL SCIENCE UNDER THE HOOD

• Live NASA data, with honesty built in: Chapter 5 requests NASA DONKI (via NASA Open APIs). If NASA does not respond, the game falls back to a snapshot that our GitHub Action saves every day, and it always tells the player which one it is showing. Static data is never called "live".

• Real orbital mechanics in the browser: the game computes today's Earth–Mars distance and message delay from JPL planetary orbit elements, so the communication delay is real on the day you play.

• Radiation the way NASA measures it: Curiosity RAD surface dose (~0.64 mSv per sol), the 2017 and 2024 storms, ISS dosimeters from NASA OSDR RadLab, and NASA OCHMO's shelter effectiveness and 600 mSv career limit. Kids see their crew's dose compared with real numbers.

• A resource simulation with power-sharing between five rooms, balanced by our own automated tester so no single strategy is always safe.

• Every number in the game links to its NASA or CSA source, or is clearly labelled "game estimate". 17 sources in total, 11 NASA fact cards.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

4. WHAT WE PUT INTO IT IN 48 HOURS (4 SPRINTS)

• 343 story lines written for the crew, NOVA and Mission Control, all of them voiced (115 audio clips, 13+ minutes)

• 75 illustrations: painted Mars scenes, a cutaway of the outpost, 12 astronaut avatars × 3 emotions (happy, worried, scared)

• ~2,700 lines of game code; weather, dust storms, day/night, aurora and particles generated in code

• 5 story chapters, 6 hands-on missions, 11 NASA fact cards, 17 cited sources

• Our own tools: a daily DONKI GitHub Action, an automated player that completes all five chapters after every change, a balance tester, and a cache-version tool so players never see a broken mix of old and new files

• Documented in four sprint reports on GitHub

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

5. BUILT WITH KIDS, FOR KIDS

Two kids on our team played every build, and we rebuilt the game after each round:

• "Too much reading" → six hands-on missions inside the story

• "Some lines are silent" → every one of the 343 lines voiced

• "The 3D faces look scary" → we dropped our 3D version for a friendly painted 2D crew

• "A separate mission mode feels disconnected" → its best parts moved into the chapters

Real players, not adults' guesses, decided what stayed in the game.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

6. HOW IT IS CREATIVE

• A game that changes with the real Sun: Chapter 5 is never the same twice.

• Trade-offs you feel, not read: the costs of every choice are shown up front, then kids do the job with their hands, and the result changes the crew's story.

• Science that admits its limits: DONKI watches space weather near Earth, and Mars can face a different side of the Sun, so the game tells kids this is practice, not a Mars forecast. We teach how scientists treat data, not just facts.

• Characters with emotions: the crew's faces react to the danger, so kids care about the people they protect.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

7. BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

• Free for every child with a browser: phones, tablets, laptops, school computers; touch or keyboard; no install.

• Accessible to 7-year-olds: every line is spoken, hard words ("sol", "EVA") can be tapped for an explanation.

• Safe by design: no ads, purchases, accounts or personal data. Only a nickname is saved, on the device.

• Ready for classrooms: a "NASA data we used" page lists every source and links CSA STEM resources and the CSA food-production toolkit for teachers and parents.

• Next: classroom playtests with teachers, discussion questions for each chapter, more NASA events (Artemis, ISS), Turkish and other languages, and an offline version for schools with weak internet.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

8. TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

Phaser 3 · JavaScript (ES modules, no build step) · HTML/CSS · Python + Google Colab (google-play-scraper, Apple Search API, pandas) · NASA Open APIs (DONKI) · GitHub + GitHub Actions · Netlify · Playwright (automated play-testing) · Kokoro-82M open-source text-to-speech

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

9. FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

• Scientific accuracy: sourced numbers, honest labels, and no AI-generated data.

• Child safety and privacy: no data collection, no images, video or voices of anyone under 18 in any material.

• Accessibility: voice for every line, simple words, works on low-end devices.

• Responsible AI use: game art was made with an AI image tool, edited by the team and watermarked "AI-generated art" on every screen; voices are synthetic and tagged in metadata; the demo narration is an ElevenLabs AI voice, stated in the video. The team designed the game, wrote the story, chose and verified every NASA dataset and ran every playtest. No NASA logos or branding were generated or modified.
